entries.abstract: A Lean 4 check, with Lean core only, of the existence of a colouring of the integers 1 to 538 with 6 colours and no monochromatic x + y = z, with x = y allowed. So the integers 1 to 538 are the union of six sum-free sets, which gives S(6) ≥ 538 for the Schur number S(6). The largest lower bound in the sources that the author read on 3 November 2026 is S(6) ≥ 537, by Chen, Zhu and Long. The paper paper/schur-six-538.md in this repository states the result.
entries.title: A Schur 6-colouring of [1, 538]

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 4.1 of A. A. Razborov and S. Rudich, Natural proofs (1997). If a generator G_k from k bits to 2k bits, computed by circuits of polynomial size, has hardness at least 2^(k^ε) for some ε > 0 and infinitely many k, then no P/poly-natural combinatorial property is useful against P/poly. The proof follows the paper. The generator gives Goldreich–Goldwasser–Micali functions of n variables with polynomial-size circuits, which a useful property must reject. The circuit that decides the large constructive subproperty then tells these functions apart from random functions. A hybrid argument over the levels of the tree and over the nodes of a level, with all other nodes fixed, gives a circuit of size 2^O(n) that tells one output of G_k apart from a uniform string with advantage 2^(-O(n)), which contradicts the hardness for n a small power of k.
entries.title: The natural proofs barrier (Razborov and Rudich)

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operator results from the local Lopatto–Rochberg manuscript. Includes analytic and coanalytic Besov classifications for every real p>0, compactness and interpolation criteria, splitting and polynomial-symbol results, and Hilbert–Schmidt energy, differential and squared-kernel quotient descriptions.
entries.title: Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operators

entries.abstract: Heisuke Hironaka's 1964 papers 'Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero I,II' were seminal achievements in the history of algebraic geometry. They had inestimable impact on a broad range of research areas in mathematics including geometry, topology, number theory, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The achievement was recognised by a Fields medal awarded to Hironaka in 1970. The papers constitute a veritable tour de force contained in 217 densely-packed pages. The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In this document, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, that is, modulo results he cites, compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works.
entries.title: HironakaLean: Hironaka's resolution of singularities (1964), formalized as written

entries.abstract: Theorem 1.1 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) bounds the sums of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] in a class modulo 4, twisted by (c/|c|)^l. The companion note extends it to g(nu, c) with any fixed numerator nu. The only new ingredient is a local identity that splits off the primes dividing nu from the coprimality conditions of the Type I Dirichlet series. This development formalizes that step from the identities of DDHL Section 3, taken as hypotheses on an abstract symbol and Gauss sum: the splitting identity g(mu, pi^k c') = (-1)^C(c', pi^k) g(mu, pi^k) g(mu pi^(2k), c') with no condition linking mu and pi, and DDHL (3.6). It proves the identity for the truncated series as an exact finite identity (Lemma 2.2), and removes pi from the coprimality condition for every valuation e = ord_pi(mu) (Corollary 2.3): on the series prime to pi the valuation reduces modulo 4; for every e the splitting has the terms k = 4j <= e and k = e + 1; and for the four exact valuations e = 1, 3 it gives single equations with an explicit finite inverse, for e = 0, 2 the coupled pair of DDHL (8.6)-(8.7). It also proves lower bounds for the determinants on Re s >= 1 and the 2-adic facts behind the signs.
entries.title: FixedNumerator: the local step in extending a theorem on quartic Gauss sums over primes to a fixed numerator

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that two-colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on rectangular grids (the paired 2-disjoint path cover problem: two vertex-disjoint paths s0 → t0 and s1 → t1 that together visit every cell) is decided by an explicit procedure, and that an explicit construction finds a solution whenever one exists. For both sides at least 11, an instance is solvable exactly when it passes a finite catalogue of forbidden patterns; for a side at most 10, a plug dynamic program decides it. The finite cases of the characterization are 21 boxes of slice certificates and 59 window certificates, all checked by the kernel.
entries.title: Two-colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on rectangles

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Kostochka–Thomason theorem, following the short proof of Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov. complete_minor_of_edges (their Theorem 1): there is d0 such that for every integer d ≥ d0, every nonempty finite simple graph with at least d·|V| edges has the complete graph K_t as a minor for every natural number t ≤ d / (10 √(ln d)). kostochka_thomason: there is a constant c > 0 such that for every integer d ≥ 2, every nonempty finite simple graph with at least d·|V| edges (average degree at least 2d) has a K_t minor for every t ≤ c·d / √(ln d). Minors are branch-set models, with the definition of the registered entry Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4, whose library is a pinned dependency. Two statements; the thresholds d0 and c are existential (the proof gives d0 = ⌈exp(R0²)⌉ + 1 with R0 ≥ 1400).
entries.title: Complete minors and average degree (Kostochka–Thomason)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical results on planar graphs and graphs without a K5 minor. (1) Wagner's theorem (1937): a finite graph is planar if and only if it has neither K5 nor K3,3 as a minor. (2) Škrekovski's theorem (1998): every finite graph without a K5 minor is 5-choosable, proved along the route of Wood and Linusson, and Thomassen's theorem (1994) that every finite planar graph is 5-choosable, as a corollary. (3) DP-colouring: every finite graph without a K5 minor (Li–Wang, 2022), hence every finite planar graph (Dvořák–Postle, 2018), is DP-5-colourable. (4) Voigt's theorem (1993): an explicit planar graph on 238 vertices with lists of four colours has no proper list colouring, so 5 cannot be lowered to 4; its planarity and non-colourability are checked by kernel reduction. (5) Wagner's equivalence of the Four Colour Theorem with Hadwiger's conjecture for K5 (neither side is proved). (6) Wagner's structure theorem (1937, added in version 2): a finite graph has no K5 minor if and only if it is a spanning subgraph of a graph obtained by clique-sums of order at most three, keeping the clique edges, from planar graphs and copies of the Wagner graph V8. Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks K4 is planar and K5, K3,3 are not.
entries.title: Wagner's planarity criterion and list colouring of planar and K5-minor-free graphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's theorem (a nonempty finite graph of average degree at least 2^(r−2) has a K_r minor), of Dirac's lemma (a graph without a K4 minor has a vertex of degree at most two, hence at most 2n − 3 edges for n ≥ 2), of Mader's bound for K5 (a graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with at least 3n − 5 edges has a K5 minor; equivalently, without a K5 minor it has at most 3n − 6 edges; added in version 2), and of Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4 (graphs without a K3 minor are 2-colourable, graphs without a K4 minor are 3-colourable). Minors are branch-set models.
entries.title: Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4

entries.abstract: For primes p = 5 (mod 16), p = a^2 + b^2 with b even, the companion note proves h(-8p) = h(-4p) + 8 [b = +-6 (mod 16)] (mod 16), which settles Conjecture 5.3 of Paper V of the K Project series. The proof writes 4(h(-8p) - h(-4p)) as a combination of representation numbers of x^2 + 2y^2 + 4z^2 and x^2 + 2y^2 + 2z^2. It shows that a weight-2 form Phi built from sieved theta series vanishes modulo 256, by Sturm's theorem and a finite check below the bound 512, and reads off the coefficient at p. This development formalizes the proof with the modular input (Serre-Stark modularity and Sturm's theorem) and Gauss's three-square class number formula as explicit hypotheses. It proves the finite check by kernel computation, the iteration of Sturm's theorem, the inversion of theta(1), the bijections relating the ternary forms to sums of three squares, the uniqueness argument for p = a^2 + b^2, the congruence, Conjecture 5.3 given Paper V Theorem 5.2(iv), and the corollaries on the octant sum and with Desnoux's congruence.
entries.title: ConjCoord: a class number congruence modulo 16 for p = 5 (mod 16) and Conjecture coord of Paper V

entries.abstract: We formalize the principal results of “Does freezing impede the growth of random recursive trees?” for uniform attachment trees with freezing. We prove uniform height lower bounds over all admissible operation sequences with n attachment steps: the height is at least e log n − 5 log log n with probability tending to one, uniformly over these sequences, and the same lower bound holds for expected height for sufficiently large n. We also formalize deletion comparisons: deleting attachment or freezing steps can increase expected height, whereas deleting the attachment–freezing pair at the first change of sign stochastically decreases height.
entries.title: Does freezing impede the growth of random recursive trees?

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Lemma 6.1 and Proposition 6.2 of H. A. Helfgott, The ternary Goldbach conjecture is true, arXiv 1312.7748v2, Section 6.1, pages 46 to 48. Lemma 6.1 is a summation by parts bound. Proposition 6.2 turns l2 bounds on S1 over the major arcs and l-infinity bounds on S2 off them into a bound for the integral of |S1|^2 |S2| over the minor arcs, without the factor log x that a plain product of norms would lose. Lemma 6.1 is stated as in the paper. Proposition 6.2 is given in three forms: an abstract measure form with a natural upper endpoint; the arcs of display 3.5 for a finite exponential polynomial S1 and a natural upper endpoint; and absolutely summable coefficients with a real upper endpoint, over any increasing measurable family of sets. The hypotheses 6.4 and 6.5 of the Proposition stay hypotheses, as in the paper, and are not proved for any exponential sum. This is one step of Helfgott's proof. The ternary Goldbach theorem itself is not formalized here, nor is Theorem 6.3 of the paper. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex and other lab agents, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Helfgott's Proposition 6.2 on the ternary Goldbach minor arcs

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof that, over a field of characteristic zero, the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n implies the Poisson conjecture in dimension n (K. Adjamagbo and A. van den Essen, 2007, Theorem 7). The statement and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (poisson_conjecture.variants.jacobian_implication in PoissonConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statement. A Poisson endomorphism's Jacobian matrix lies in Mathlib's symplectic group, so its determinant is a unit; the Jacobian conjecture then gives a polynomial inverse.
entries.title: The Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n implies the Poisson conjecture in dimension n

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that for every ε > 0 and all large natural x there is a Goldbach number, an even sum of two primes, in the interval from x to x + 3 x^(26/1075+ε). The theorem is conditional on two cited results taken as explicit hypotheses, never as axioms, and neither is proved here: LiRow052, R. Li, arXiv 2308.04458, Theorem 2, the row θ = 0.52, primes in the intervals from n - n^(0.52+ε) to n with a lower bound of the right order, with some positive constant since the printed constant differs between versions of the paper; and LiPrintedExceptionalCount, R. Li, arXiv 2407.05651 v6, Theorem 1.1, primes in the intervals from n to n + n^(1/21.5+ε) for almost all n. The argument adapts Theorem 7.1 of arXiv 2407.05651 v6, page 27, exponent 21/860 from the 0.525 of Baker, Harman and Pintz. The exponent 26/1075 is lower by 1/4300, and the gain is only the replacement of 0.525 by Li's 0.52. Li prints this exponent himself, as Theorem 7 of arXiv 2308.04458, with no ε and no factor 3, so this is a formal check of a known result and not a new exponent. Li's later note, Primes in almost all short intervals II, claims 1/22+ε in place of 1/21.5+ε, so 26/1075 is not claimed as the best exponent. Both cited papers are used here in their arXiv preprint form. Proved with no cited input: the passage from a count of primes in the intervals below n to a count in the windows from x - 2Y to x - Y, and the combinatorial step from the two counts to a Goldbach number. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex and Gemini, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Goldbach numbers in short intervals of length x^(26/1075+ε)

entries.abstract: For generalized k-server, each named server moves in its own metric space, a request specifies one point per space, and matching any coordinate serves the request. The development proves a height-k tower lower bound on the deterministic competitive ratio on k real lines for k at least three, allowing arbitrary additive constants. It also proves existence of a lazy deterministic algorithm on arbitrary metric spaces with arbitrary positive movement weights and prescribed initial configuration, with an explicit factor depending only on k and no additive cost or horizon input. The refined deterministic factor is at most tower(k+4) for k at least two.
entries.title: Deterministic generalized k-server: tower lower bound and strict upper bound

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the chordal results of the author's preprint "Clique partitions with rooted simplicial defect: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds" (Erdős #81 series, Paper IV). With M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋: there is b such that every chordal graph on n vertices has a clique partition into pieces of order at most four with at most M(n) + b pieces (Theorem A); for n large every chordal graph on n vertices has one with at most M(n) pieces, and some chordal graph on n vertices has one with exactly M(n) pieces that is optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem B, the bound asked in Erdős Problem #81 and its sharpness); 1/6 is the least quadratic coefficient (§6.3); the uniform mixed rounding of fractional triangle/K₄ packings (Theorem 3.1); integral stability with explicit constants and edit distance at most 16δ to a complete-split graph, for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn² with γ = 10⁻¹⁶/4 (Theorem 6.1); same-root control of near-optimal partitions: one clique root satisfies all the conclusions of Theorem 6.1 and, for it, every partition with at most M(n) + τ pieces has at most τ + 48δ noncanonical pieces (Corollary 6.1a); the root-defect identity (6.7b); and the eventual classification of the extremal chordal graphs as complete-split graphs with a core of optimal size (Corollary 6.2). Version 2 adds the fixed-defect results for graphs of rooted simplicial defect at most s: the sharp eventual bound Q_s(n) = M(n + s) − C(s + 1, 2), attained by a partition optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem C); same-root stability with A_s = 2·10⁴¹·(s + 1)⁸ for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn², edit distance at most A_s δ, at most τ + (1 + 7A_s)δ noncanonical pieces carrying at most 10τ + 10(1 + 7A_s)δ edges (Theorem C′); comparison with an optimal-size template at distance at most A_s δ + n√((1 + 4A_s)δ) and the equality case cp = c₄ = Q_s(n) (Corollary 6.3); the necessity of the square-root term (Proposition 6.3a); the bounds F₄(G) ≤ M(n − s) + ns (minus C(s + 1, 2) when 4s ≤ n) and their integral form up to εn² (Proposition 6.4); the sublinear-defect bound n²/6 + o(n²) and root stability (Theorem 6.5); the bound Q_s(n) for all s ≤ S once n ≥ T(P(S)), an explicit tower (Corollary 6.6); and the annex inequality: a chordal K_{d+2}-free graph has fractional triangle packing number at most ν₃ + (10 + d/2)n (G.1). 21 statements. The thresholds N and γ in Theorems B, C, C′ and Corollary 6.3 are existential; b, N, A_s and the tower are not claimed optimal.
entries.title: Clique partitions of chordal graphs: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds

entries.abstract: Over the group algebra F2[C4] of the cyclic group of order four in characteristic two, we give an explicit five-stage real-indexed persistence diagram F of unbounded chain complexes. Its stages are shifts of the periodic free resolution of the trivial module, on half-open intervals [i, i+1), with zero diagram before time 0 and from time 5 on. We compare three distances from F to the zero diagram: the homology interleaving distance (supremum over all degrees of the interleaving distances of the F2-homology persistence modules); the interleaving distance in an arbitrary localisation of the category of whole real diagrams at the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms (the derived category of real diagrams); and the strict homotopy-interleaving distance, which allows arbitrary finite zigzags of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of both entire diagrams, including nonzero acyclic replacements of zero. The Lean development proves d_CohI(F,0) = 1/2 < d_IHC(F,0) = 1 < 5/4 <= d_HI(F,0) <= 5/2. So the three distances are quantitatively separated by a single explicit example. The lower bound for the strict metric comes from a fourfold defining-system obstruction for the resolution. The derived upper bound comes from a natural nullhomotopy of the two-unit shift. The upper bound 5/2 for the strict metric is witnessed directly, because every five-unit shift of F vanishes.
entries.title: A quantitative homotopy-interleaving gap over the cyclic-four group algebra

entries.abstract: Let P be a nonempty set of propositional variables. The freely generated zero-identity Boolean category B(P) of Došen and Petrić is maximal: every congruence on its morphisms preserved by the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution is either equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. The formalization gives two proofs of maximality and proves the congruence dichotomy. It also proves that the identity and zero endomorphism of each variable are distinct, and that there is no morphism from the terminal object to the initial object.
entries.title: Maximality of the Došen–Petrić Boolean Category

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main theorem of R. Montgomery, "Fractional clique decompositions of dense partite graphs" (arXiv:1603.01039; Combin. Probab. Comput. 26 (2017)): for r ≥ 3, every balanced K_r-divisible r-partite graph with parts of size n in which every vertex has at least (1 − 1/(10⁶r³))n neighbours in every other part has a fractional K_r-decomposition (Theorem 1.1); and its non-partite consequence: every graph on n vertices with minimum degree at least (1 − 1/(10⁶r³))n has a fractional K_r-decomposition. The whole proof is formalized: clique counts (Proposition 3.2, Lemma 3.3), the two gadgets (Lemmas 4.2, 4.3), the splitting lemma (Lemma 4.4), the moving lemmas (Lemmas 5.2, 5.3, 5.6) and the final averaging. Not formalized: Theorem 1.2 (integral decompositions), which also needs the fractional-to-exact transfer of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor.
entries.title: Fractional clique decompositions of dense partite graphs

entries.abstract: For a prime p let a = v_2(p-1), m = (p-1)/2^a, H_a the subgroup of (Z/p)^x of order m and s(x) = (-1)^<x>. The development proves the tower of band-parity laws of Paper I of the author's series: the cyclotomic tower (every coordinate of the band-parity sum of the character of order 2^a is congruent modulo 4 to an explicit count), the band-parity tower f_a = sum over H_a of s(u) s(u^2) = m (mod 4) at every odd prime, the doubling count sum over 2H_a of s(u) s(2u) = 2 N_a - m, the imaginary law e_a = 2 N_a - m (mod 4) at every prime p = 1 (mod 4) with its level-3 form, the collapse e_a = +-f_a when 2 is a 2^(a-1)-th power residue, and E. Lehmer's criterion for 2 to be a 2k-th power residue. It also proves the power-map family, the companion law Re C = Im C = kappa (mod 4) at p = 1 (mod 8), and Lehmer-type invariants of the inversion map modulo 4; and, modulo 8, the joint-parity form, the dichotomy, squaring cycles and the order-three pair, the defect lemma, odd multipliers as floor sums and the fifth-interval formula linking M_H(5) to B_{1,theta_p}.
entries.title: BandParityTower: the band-parity tower and its limit modulo eight

entries.abstract: If A \ F is a basis for every finite set F and A has positive lower density, then A has a restricted order: every sufficiently large integer is a sum of a bounded number of distinct elements of A. This is a partial result on Erdős Problem 338 (Erdős and Graham ask whether every such A, without the density condition, has a restricted order). The proof counts pairs to show that, for every R, the numbers with at least R representations as a sum of two distinct elements of A have positive lower density, uniformly in R; uses Kneser's theorem for finite abelian groups to write all large numbers of one residue class as sums of a bounded number of such numbers; fixes the residue class with distinct elements of A; and chooses the representations greedily so that all summands are distinct.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 338: restricted order of robust sets of positive lower density

entries.abstract: For an integer r >= 2 and a finite set N of primes, the random Euler product model for Dirichlet characters of order r replaces chi(q) by independent uniform r-th roots of unity. The development proves that the order-r local factor E|1 - z/q|^(-2) equals (1 + q^-r)/((1 - q^-2)(1 - q^-r)), that its ratio to the full-circle factor (1 - q^-2)^(-1), multiplied over the primes outside N, is zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r), that this correction factor is also the sum of (ab)^-r over the coprime pairs of integers prime to N, and that the model mean is zeta^(N)(2) zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r). The factor exceeds 1, decreases strictly in r and tends to 1; for r = 2k and N empty it equals -binom(4k,2k) B_{2k}^2/(2 B_{4k}). For r = 4 and N = {2} it is 35/34, the ratio by which the limit of Louboutin's mean square of L(1, chi) with the factor at 2 removed changes when the average is restricted to quartic characters; with the forced factor 4/5 at 2 the development also proves the constants pi^2/10, 7 pi^2/68, 7 pi^2/36 and 7/136 = (1/20)(35/34) = (7/72)(9/17). It also identifies the pairs the model keeps: for positive m, n the average of z^m conj(z^n) is 1 exactly when m/n is an r-th power in Q, that is when (m, n) = (d a^r, d b^r) with a, b coprime, and 0 otherwise. Modulo a single prime p with r | p - 1 it proves the finite-character counterpart: there are exactly r Dirichlet characters mod p with chi^r = 1, the sum of chi(a) conj(chi(b)) over them is r when a/b is a nonzero r-th power mod p and 0 otherwise, so every pair (d a^r, d b^r) prime to p survives with sum r; by contrast, summed over all characters mod p, chi(m) conj(chi(n)) has sum 0 for distinct m, n < p. Release v1.2 adds the finite part of the Chebyshev bias in families p = a (mod M) of fixed order r: with rho_s(t) the average of exp(2 pi i u t/s) over the units u mod s, the sum over t < s of rho_s(c t) is s when s | c and 0 otherwise; for M > 0 and s | M the squares in Z/s x| (Z/M)^x give the prime-square term of the explicit formula as s times the square-root count beta(M, a, s) = #{y in (Z/M)^x : y^2 = a, y = -1 (mod s)}, a count of residue classes (the same finite-sum identity over the representatives 0 <= x < M holds for all M and s > 0, but is only an arithmetic identity there: vacuous at M = 0, representative-dependent when s does not divide M); beta does not decrease as s decreases along divisibility, at s = r it is 0 unless a is a square in H = ker((Z/M)^x -> (Z/r)^x) and is then the number of square roots of 1 in H; and for the imaginary families (r even, M = 2r, a = 1 + r) beta vanishes for every s unless 8 | r, and for s = r/d with d odd in every case.
entries.title: FixedOrderFactor: the order-r correction factor for mean squares of L(1, chi), and the factor 35/34

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Green's paper Counting sets with small sumset, and the clique number of random Cayley graphs. For a finite abelian group Γ, let S_k^m(Γ) be the family of the sets X in Γ with |X| = k whose restricted sumset X ∔ X = {x + y : x, y in X, x ≠ y} has m elements. The paper bounds |S_k^m(Γ)| for Γ = Z/NZ and Γ = F_2^n, through a bound for the number of Freiman isomorphism classes of sets with small restricted sumset in a vector space. It deduces that the Cayley sum graph of a random subset of Z/NZ almost surely has clique number at most 160 log_2 N, and that the Cayley graph of a random subset of F_2^n almost surely has clique number between C_1 n log_2 n and C_2 n log_2 n. The formalization proves these results with C_1 = 1/4 and C_2 = 308, both as limits and as explicit bounds on the number of exceptional sets.

The development proves this Mellin duality over any commutative ring, its inversion over the odd complex characters and its form bilinear in first Bernoulli numbers, the half-sum identity, the exponent family and its two collapses. entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of ten statements. Let K be a number field of degree 9 containing a totally real cubic field L and a cubic field M with one real place. Then K = LM has signature (3, 3), and its nine embeddings are the pairs (lambda, mu). A slot assignment, fixed by a labelling of L's embeddings and a non-real embedding mu_1 of M, places the nine conjugates of x in K in a 3 x 3 Hermitian array, the symbol of x; the symbol of x^-1 is its entrywise (Hadamard) inverse. (1) For every finite index type, a positive semidefinite complex matrix with no zero entry has positive semidefinite Hadamard inverse iff it is w w* (rank one); (2) for every complex matrix with no zero entry (positive semidefiniteness not assumed), the Schur multipliers of the matrix and of its Hadamard inverse are both completely positive iff it is w w*. Statements 1-2 are supporting lemmas. (3) The setting: L and M are linearly disjoint, L M = K, and K has 3 real and 3 complex places. (4) The slot assignment exists, is a bijection Fin 3 x Fin 3 ~ (K -> C) with real diagonal and conjugate-symmetric slots, and is unique. (5) For x != 0 in K, the symbol of x is rank one iff N_{K/L}(x) and N_{K/M}(x) are one and the same positive rational number. (6) For a unit u, the symbol is rank one iff N_{K/L}(u) = N_{K/M}(u) = 1. (7) These units H are torsion-free and their logarithmic embedding spans a Z-module of rank 2, so H is isomorphic to Z^2 (the isomorphism is not itself a Lean term). (8) For a unit u, the Schur multipliers of the symbols of u and of u^-1 are both completely positive iff u is in H. (9) There is a unit of infinite order all of whose powers run both ways. (10) The degree-four contrast: in a field with two real places and one complex place, both Schur multipliers of the 2 x 2 place symbol of a unit u and of u^-1 are completely positive iff u is positive at both real places and |sigma(u)| = 1. Statements 4-6, 8 and 9 hold for every labelling and every non-real mu_1. The compositum place bookkeeping is ported, with citation, from the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012; it is not re-proved. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by a unit; if a unit acts by multiplication on a Hermitian register of its places and an admissible tick must be completely positive, then in degree four a tick u != 1 runs both ways only through a conjugate on the unit circle (Salem type); in a field such as Q(Q), Q^4 = Q + 1, the only such elements are +-1 (not proved in this entry; it follows from statement 17 of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, since Q(Q) is contained in Q(rho, Q)), so there the arithmetic gives time a direction; in degree nine a rank-two group of units runs both ways, so the direction is not a property of arithmetic in general: it rests on the degree-four shape and on Q(Q) having no conjugate on the unit circle. The ticks are completely positive, not trace-non-increasing. Companion of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), whose README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.
entries.title: The Arithmetic of Time: reversible units of a degree-nine field. The units of K = LM (L, M cubic) with rank-one Hermitian symbol are exactly those of trivial relative norm to L and to M, a group of rank two, and exactly those whose Schur multipliers run both ways

entries.abstract: Conjecture 1.2 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) asserts that the sums S_beta(X; l) of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] with N(c) <= X and c = beta (mod 4), twisted by (conj(c)/|c|)^l and weighted by the von Mangoldt function, are b_beta X^(3/4) + O(X^(1/2+eps)) with b_beta nonzero when l = 0 and O(X^(1/2+eps)) when l is nonzero. The development proves that if g(c)^2 = -kappa c/|c| for a fixed unit kappa on the support of the weight (the identity (1.2) of the same paper), then g(c) conj(c)/|c| = -kappa conj(g(c)), so S_beta(X; 1) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; 0)), and the cases l = 0 and l = 1 of the conjecture force b_beta = 0, which the conjecture excludes; the same holds when the identity fails on an exceptional set of weight O(X^(1/2+eps)). More generally S_beta(X; 1 - l) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; l)) for every l. The corrected conjecture, with main term -kappa conj(b_beta) X^(3/4) at l = 1, is shown equivalent under the identity to its cases l <= 0, and that main term is shown to be the only one compatible with the case l = 0. It also proves the pairing identities A(nu^3, -m) = -kappa conj A(nu, m) for the twisted moments and the fact behind the special role of order four: if |g| = 1 and g^k = xi then conj(g) = g^(k-1) conj(xi). The Gauss sum and the von Mangoldt function are abstract functions on the Gaussian integers, so no quartic residue symbol is defined.
entries.title: QuarticPairing: the pairing of the twists in Conjecture 1.2 of David, Dunn, Hamieh and Lin

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two theorems of Fabrici and Jendrol' (1997), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. Theorem 1 (light_path): a 3-connected planar graph that contains a path on k ≥ 1 vertices contains such a path whose vertices all have degree at most 5k. Theorem 2 (only_paths_light): for every connected planar graph H that is not a path (not isomorphic to pathGraph on its vertex count) and every m, there is a 3-connected planar graph containing a copy of H in which every copy of H (an injective edge-preserving map) has a vertex of degree at least m. Two statements. Theorem 1 follows the proof reproduced in the Jendrol'–Voss survey (maximal counterexample, chords at major vertices, a major vertex with at most five major neighbours). Theorem 2 uses a different construction from the article's: H is completed to an edge-maximal planar graph, whose faces are triangles, and two chains of repeated stellations are inserted in every face, so that the light vertices induce disjoint paths; the result is a plane triangulation, hence 3-connected. entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the mathematics of Y. Saouter, Checking the odd Goldbach conjecture up to 10^20, Math. Comp. 67, 1998, 863 to 866. Proved with no hypothesis: Lemma 1, the paper's form of Theorem 5 of Brillhart, Lehmer and Selfridge 1975, for every even F; Theorem 1, the primality criterion for N = 2^22 R + 1 below 10^20 with R odd and any base a with a^((N-1)/2) = -1 modulo N; Lemma 2 by quadratic reciprocity; Theorem 2, the case of base 5; the primality of the 100 rungs of Table 1 and of the first and last primes printed in the paper. The printed ladder constant 1258213 is a misprint for 12582913, and this repair is proved. The entry does not reverify Saouter's computation: his ladder of about 250 million rungs is checked only through its first 100 rungs. As a derived result, not a theorem of the paper, every odd number from 7 to 10^20 is a sum of three primes, conditional on one cited input taken as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom: EvenGoldbachUpTo of 4 * 10^18, the published computation of T. Oliveira e Silva, S. Herzog and S. Pardi, Math. Comp. 83, 2014, not proved here. That proof uses Saouter's prime ladder with 25 Proth rungs as in Helfgott and Platt, so the paper's range is reproduced by a different ladder on a much larger even input than Saouter's 4 * 10^11. Ternary Goldbach for all odd numbers is Helfgott's theorem, from his 2013 preprint, and is not formalized here. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, which is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Checking the odd Goldbach conjecture up to 10^20

entries.abstract: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate. These are the three compared statements of the registered record (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 at revision c48eb12), unchanged in this revision. The uniqueness results proved in this repository (Supplement.lean: padovan_minimal_unique, padovan_eigenvalue_unique, padovan_matrix_unique, pisot_ge_plastic, padovan_rules_chiral) are registered separately as PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 (stalex444/arithmetic-of-time-slowest-clock, revision 49eafbab4af8899b2a66469697bf74683a88ce87), which compares them over s, mir, inc and sub. Everything else in this repository is public and kernel-checked but not compared: among it the exact orientation threshold (padovan_exact_orientation_threshold_four), the irrationality of the distinguished slope (Time.beta_irrational), mirror identities for arbitrary substitutions, a rate identity, and the characteristic polynomial and chirality of a twelve-letter substitution for ρQ.
entries.title: The Arithmetic of Time: chirality of the Padovan substitution

entries.abstract: Let f(n) be the least m >= 1 such that n! = a_1 ... a_t with a_1 < ... < a_t = a_1 + m. Assuming the abc conjecture, f(n) tends to infinity. The proof follows Luca's proof that abc implies finitely many solutions of P(x) = n!, for the polynomials prod_{i in T} (x + i): for a fixed set T of d offsets, the shift y = d a + sum(T) gives d^d prod_{i in T} (a + i) = y^d + y^k R(y) with k + deg R <= d - 2 and R(0) != 0, and abc, with rad(n!) <= 4^n, bounds y by an exponential in n, while y^d >= n!. It does not assume Luca's theorem; only the reduction from f(n) to these polynomials is specific to Problem 393.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 393: f(n) tends to infinity, assuming the abc conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 of Madaras (2004), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. In every plane map of a finite simple graph of minimum degree at least three whose faces all have length at least five, some vertex x of degree three has three distinct neighbours a, b, c with deg a = deg b = 3 and deg c ≤ 4 (light_star3); in particular the star K1,3 is light, with degree sum at most 13. In the same setting, some face of length five shares an edge with a face of length at most six such that all vertices of both faces have degree at most nine (light_pair; the two faces may coincide when the graph is not 2-connected). Two statements. The proof of Theorem 1.1 is a discharging argument on the rotation system with charges deg − 4 and ℓ − 4 in which every face gives each corner at a 3-vertex a weight depending only on the degrees of the two neighbours along the face, and vertices of degree at least five give 1/5 to each 3-neighbour; the local inequalities are checked by decide in the kernel. This replaces the article's transfer of charge between adjacent 3-vertices. Theorem 1.3 is proved by a second discharging with charges 2 deg − 6 and ℓ − 6: vertices give their charge to their corners, and every face gives 1/5 across each edge to an adjacent poor face (length five, all degrees at most five, at most one of degree at least four).

A Gauss-Lehmer product argument gives the quartic Gauss lemma w = (-1)^(R_1 + R_3) for the quarter counts R_r, the parity of the four quarter counts when w = 1, and the parity of R_2 through the order of 2. For the quarter sum Omega = x + iy (2N(Omega) = h^-(K) for the imaginary cyclic quartic field K of conductor 4p, not formalized) it proves criteria in the quarter counts for 2^k | 2N(Omega), 2 <= k <= 6, a classical evaluation of the fourth, the coordinate valuation formula, a congruence modulo 16 linking c0 - c1 to x - y, and the valuation of B_(2,chi) at 1 + i on its first three cases.

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Kac's return-time formula. For a measure-preserving map f and a measurable set A, the integral over A of the first return time to A equals the measure of the points whose orbit ever meets A. The return time is valued in the extended naturals, infinite for a point that never returns, and with that convention the formula holds for every measure, with no finiteness, sigma-finiteness, conservativity or ergodicity assumption. For an ergodic map of a probability space and mu(A) > 0 the integral is 1, so the mean return time to A, starting in A, is 1 / mu(A).
entries.title: Kac's return-time formula for any measure-preserving map

entries.abstract: Erdős asked whether a set of n points in the plane with no isosceles triangle must determine at least f(n)n distinct distances for some f(n) tending to infinity, and asked the same in R^k for each fixed k. Straus observed that no such bound holds uniformly in the dimension. In the form stated in formal-conjectures: for every k there are 2^k points in R^k with no isosceles triangle and at most 2^k - 1 distinct distances. This formalization proves that statement, using the points whose i-th coordinate is 0 or sqrt(2^i); the sources consulted do not record Straus's own construction.

entries.abstract: Erdős asked whether, for every set of n points in the plane with no four on a circle, some point has at least (1 - o(1))n distinct distances to the other points. Feng et al. (arXiv:2601.22401; construction found by their agent Aletheia) answered no, using 4m points on the coordinate axes at powers of 2 and 3. This formalization proves the negative answer and their statement (for every m >= 10 there are 4m points, no four on a circle, each with at most 3m - 1 distinct distances to the other points), using a different set on the same axes: (±2i, 0) and (0, ±(2j - 1)) for 1 <= i, j <= m. An auxiliary lemma gives the bound for every m >= 1.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Lavery, "Discrete Beurling number systems with integer error below every power of x and no zero-free half-plane". The headline theorem, BModel.one_zero_system_exists, constructs a discrete Beurling generalized number system whose integer counting function satisfies N(x) = x + O_ε(x^ε) for every ε > 0, while its zeta function is zero-free on no half-plane Re s > 1 − ε (a discrete [1, 0]-system in the sense of Broucke–Debruyne–Révész). The second theorem, BModel.corollary_2_2_complete, is Corollary 2.2: the answer to Question Q (must N(x) = Ax + O(x^θ) with θ < 1/2 force a zero-free half-plane?) is negative. The project also proves Theorem A for every θ ∈ (0, 1/2 − 10⁻⁴]: a system with N(x) = x + O(x^θ log* x) whose zeta function has zeros ρ_k with 1 − Re ρ_k = (log log x_k + O(1))/log x_k, i.e. at distance 1·log log x_k / log x_k from the line Re s = 1. The method is integer-first: a randomised greedy rule chooses each generalized prime so that the integer count tracks a target x + R(x) whose oscillation R plants the zeros; the main work is a positive drift for the queue of composites at every scale, using a Beurling–Saias-type resolvent bound, a local prime number theorem for the realised system and a cluster-counting theorem, with numerical certificates checked by the Lean kernel (decide +kernel). In Lean both theorems are conditional on one explicit hypothesis, BaseRange.Huxley84, eq. (84) of the paper: a short-interval prime number theorem for the rational primes (relative error ≤ (log q)⁻³ on every interval of length ≥ (2q)^{7/12} in [q, 2q], for large q). This is a known theorem (Heath-Brown 1988 with the de la Vallée Poussin error term) that is not in Mathlib; it is a hypothesis of the theorems, not an axiom. The paper and the formalization were produced with heavy AI assistance (Claude agents; the Lean development was started by Aristotle, Harmonic) and have had no human expert review.
entries.title: Discrete Beurling number systems with integer error below every power, without a zero-free half-plane (assuming the short-interval prime number theorem (84))

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of a weighted independent-set existence bound for finite clique-free graphs. For every integer r at least four, positive real degree weights s, and nonnegative real objective weights a, a K_r-free graph has an independent set whose a-weight is at least c_r times the sum of a_v f(s(N(v))/s_v), where f is Shearer's function. The coefficient is the explicit positive rational c_r = 1/(1 + 1152 B_0 r), with a fixed absolute constant B_0, and has proved upper and lower bounds of order 1/r. The proof combines scalar potentials, a weighted triangle dichotomy, sparse neighborhood restriction, deletion identities, and compactness induction.
entries.title: Weighted independent sets in clique-free graphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the sharp Hamiltonicity threshold of the binomial random graph: if ω(n) → ∞, then G(n, (log n + log log n + ω(n))/n) is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 1, and G(n, (log n + log log n − ω(n))/n) is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 0 (Komlós–Szemerédi 1983; Bollobás 1984). The edge probability is clipped to [0, 1] (min 1 above, max 0 below). The statements are given in the finite product model of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-28-000021 (one independent Bernoulli(p) coin per pair of distinct vertices of Fin n) and, as corollaries, for Mathlib's SimpleGraph.binomialRandom with the edge probability projected to [0, 1]. Hamiltonicity is Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian.
entries.title: The Hamiltonicity threshold of the random graph G(n, p) (Komlós–Szemerédi)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Corollary 1.6 for r = 3 of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor, "Clique decompositions of multipartite graphs and completion of Latin squares" (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 151 (2017), arXiv:1603.01043): fractional triangle decompositions above a threshold give triangle decompositions above the same threshold. Precisely: if δ ≥ 3/4 and, for every ε > 0, every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with three parts of size n ≥ n₀(ε) and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a fractional triangle decomposition, then for every ε > 0 there is n₀ such that every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with parts of size n ≥ n₀ and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a triangle decomposition (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6). The hypothesis δ ≥ 3/4 is an extra assumption of the Lean statement: the article does not need it because the fractional threshold is known to be at least 3/4, which is not formalized here. Combined with the fractional bound of Allsop, Bowtell, Lesgourgues and Petrova (pinned entry PALOMAR-2026-10-30-000008), this gives the unconditional statement with threshold 0.769 − 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6_ablp). The proof follows the iterative absorption of the article (absorbers, vortex of partitions with random reserves, cover-down, balancing graph, assembly) but replaces the regularity-based Section 8 by a route through the fractional threshold and the Haxell–Rödl transfer. Version 2 adds Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 3.2 for r = 3, the completion of partial Latin squares: for every ε > 0 and all large n, every partial Latin square of order n in which every row, every column and every symbol is used at most (1 − δ − ε)n times extends to a Latin square, above the fractional threshold δ ≥ 3/4 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4, from Cor16 δ by BKLOT2017.corollary_3_2) and unconditionally with 1 − δ = 0.231 + 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4_ablp).
entries.title: Triangle decompositions of dense tripartite graphs and completion of partial Latin squares

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Borodin's theorem on light triangles, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of a triangle is the sum of the degrees of its vertices. Every plane map of a graph of minimum degree at least five has a face of length three of weight at most 17 (light_face), and hence a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a triangle of weight at most 17 (light_triangle). Two statements. The proof is a discharging argument run on the rotation system, with face charges in place of an edge-maximal counterexample; the local analysis at 5-vertices (32768 configurations of neighbour degrees capped at eight and corner types) is checked by decide in the kernel.
entries.title: Borodin's light triangles in planar graphs of minimum degree five

entries.abstract: Lean proof that the forward uniform-attachment/freezing construction and the reversed growth-coalescent construction give the same distribution of labelled rooted trees, after the prescribed erasure of active reverse labels. The equality includes the extinction endpoint. It is stated on a canonical encoding that retains the complete graph and relevant labels. The dictionary to literal isomorphism-class language is mathematically reviewed but is not an additional Lean quotient-law equivalence theorem. This entry covers T05 and shares its proof repository with the companion asymptotic and SIR entries.
entries.title: Uniform attachment with freezing: equivalence in law of the forward and reversed constructions

entries.abstract: Lean proofs of the four Introduction theorems of Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declumping, including periodic offspring laws. Secondary results, proof departures, manuscript corrections and remaining background obligations are recorded in FORMALIZATION_REPORT.md.
entries.title: Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declumping

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps and no hypotheses, of explicit two-sided bounds for Chebyshev's function psi from P. L. Chebyshev, Mémoire sur les nombres premiers, 1852, with Chebyshev's constant A = log 2/2 + log 3/3 + log 5/5 - log 30/30 = 0.92129.... For every natural number n at least 30, psi of n is at least A n - 5 log n + 2 log 30 - 1; for every natural number n, psi of n is at most 6A/5 n + 2 log^2 n + 160. The proof uses Chebyshev's combination of log n!, log of the factorials of n/2, n/3 and n/5, and log of the factorial of n/30, as in the paper, with error terms weaker than Chebyshev's. Mathlib has Chebyshev type bounds only with the constants log 2 and log 4. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit. Goldbach's conjecture is open and is not claimed.
entries.title: Mémoire sur les nombres premiers

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kotzig's theorem on light edges and its relatives, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of an edge uv is deg u + deg v. A planar graph of minimum degree at least three has an edge of weight at most 13 (kotzig_borodin; the form without 3-connectivity conjectured by Erdős and proved by Borodin); a planar graph of minimum degree at least four has an edge of weight at most 11 (light_edge_minDegree_four); Kotzig's theorem (1955): a 3-connected planar graph has an edge of weight at most 13, and at most 11 if it has no vertex of degree three (kotzig); Wernicke's theorem (1904): a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a vertex of degree five adjacent to a vertex of degree at most six (wernicke). Four statements. The proof is a discharging argument carried out directly on the rotation system, without triangulating.
entries.title: Kotzig's theorem on light edges of planar graphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of A. W. Dudek, On the Riemann hypothesis and the difference between primes, Int. J. Number Theory 11, 2015, arXiv 1402.6417. Each theorem is conditional on the Riemann hypothesis, the paper's own hypothesis, stated with Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis. Theorem 2: for every real x at least 2 there is a prime in the interval from x - (4/pi) sqrt(x) log x to x. Theorem 1: there is c > 0 such that the interval from x to x + c sqrt(x) log x holds more than sqrt(x) primes for every real x at least 2. Theorem 3: for every epsilon > 0 and all large x there is a prime in the interval from x - (1 + epsilon) sqrt(x) log x to x. Each theorem also takes one cited input as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom: HSWN70 gZ, the zero count of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, arXiv 2107.06506, Corollary 1.2, for T at least 70, stated for gZ, the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function counted with multiplicity. The paper cites the zero count of Trudgian 2014 at this point, whose constant Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong report to be in error; the corrected count is used instead. The bounds of Schoenfeld 1976 for psi - theta, which the paper also cites, are not an input here: the needed estimate is proved. Dudek's Lemma 4 and the explicit formula for psi_1 are proved as well. An AI agent, Claude, wrote the Lean code, with the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: On the Riemann hypothesis and the difference between primes

entries.abstract: For the powerful part Q_2(m) of m, this formalization proves that limsup Q_2(n(n+1)...(n+l))/n^2 is infinite for every l >= 2 (the second question of Erdős Problem 935), and at least 1 for every l >= 1 (a consequence of a result of Mahler noted by Erdős). Both use solutions of the Pell equation x^2 = 8y^2 + 1.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 935: powerful parts of products of consecutive integers
